source: Persistence Athletics scouting reads. Grounded strictly in the current computed intel (placement percentiles, energy systems, self-reported benchmarks, Games history) for the full field of 81 (46 confirmed qualifiers + 35 contenders). No claim appears that is not in the data; relative weaknesses are framed as relative. Authored to the fact-checked, no-fabrication, no-AI-tells standard.
note: Keyed by projection slug. Regenerate when the field locks (~June 16).

narratives.colten-mertens: Mertens tops the contender board at #1 of 41 on the strength of a field-best 555 lb back squat and balanced gymnastics and weightlifting, both around the 53rd percentile. The exposure is the engine and the bodyweight grind, metabolic at 43rd and bodyweight at 23rd, with a thin phosphagen read of 43. Four Games trips, best of 12th. He still has to punch through the online Semifinal, and a long aerobic floor is where he leaks.
narratives.peter-ellis: Ellis sits #14 and the read is modest: a 40th-percentile long engine is his one lane, anchored by a 2nd in Open 26.3, but everything fast or heavy is a hole, Heavy at 13th and Sprint at 15th with phosphagen down at 29. Two Games trips, best of 28th. A contender still fighting in, he needs the tests long and the loads light to climb.
narratives.jeffrey-adler: The engine is why the model has him 2nd of 41: 95th-percentile long engine, 90th metabolic, and a Filthy 50 best in the field. Straight running is the soft spot, a 19:15 5k that lands near the bottom of reporters, and sprint and gymnastics, though still high at 75th and 78th, are his relative edges. A 73 consistency and a 2023 title say he wins on a long, grippy floor.
narratives.jay-crouch: Crouch climbs to 3rd on an 85th-percentile long engine and a steady 76 consistency, the profile of a man who keeps stacking finishes. Heavy and sprint work, both in the high 60s, are his softer rooms, so he is rarely the one to win a barbell sprint but rarely loses ground either. Six Games deep with a 6th best, the engine keeps him in the title math.
narratives.harry-lightfoot: Lightfoot lands 4th on an 88th-percentile engine and 80th gymnastics, the same lane that carried him through Quarterfinals. Speed is the relative gap, Sprint at 55th and metabolic at 68th, both still respectable, so he is not fast but seldom slow. A 79.9 consistency holds him steady when the weekend grinds, and a contender's path opens if the tests run long and mixed.
narratives.james-sprague: Sprague's separator is the engine, not the iron: 93rd-percentile metabolic, 90th bodyweight, and best-in-field CHAD1000x, Fight Gone Bad and Grace to prove the gas tank. The barbell is the relative soft spot, Heavy at 63rd and Weightlifting at 75th, so a max-effort day is where the field claws even. Three Games trips with a 2024 win on the card. Anywhere the clock keeps running, he is a problem.
narratives.dallin-pepper: Pepper is built for the heavy and the short: 93rd-percentile gymnastics and 85th sprint, with a best-in-field 385 lb clean and jerk and a 495 lb squat. The long grind is the trade, Long Engine at 75th and a Fight Gone Bad that lands last of the reporters, so an aerobic chipper can stall him. A 2nd-place Games finish on the card and the model at 6th. He wins when the barbell is heavy and the pieces stay quick.
narratives.jonne-koski: Ten Games trips and not a panic button in sight. Koski sits 7th with bodyweight and long-engine work in the high 70s, the lanes that have kept him in the mix since 2014. The barbell is the soft spot, Heavy at 60th and a 345 lb clean and jerk near the bottom of reporters, so a heavy day costs him ground he claws back on the engine. A contender who wins by never leaking points.
narratives.jayson-hopper: Hopper's weapon is power: Sprint at 78th and Heavy at 83rd, with a 585 lb deadlift second in the field and a 0:52 400m. The barbell-cycling benchmarks are the tell on the other side, a 2:15 Fran and a 2:00 Grace both near the bottom, so a high-skill engine grinder is where he leaks. The model has him 8th with a 2025 Games win on the card, and on a heavy, fast floor he beats that.
narratives.justin-medeiros: Medeiros has no real hole. His strongest rooms are Heavy and Sprint at the 98th percentile, the short loaded explosive work, but even his relatively weakest domains, Bodyweight and Long Engine, still sit 83rd to 100th in this field. A 79.8 consistency says he does not give events away. Two Games titles on the card, and the model's 9th seed reads low for a profile this complete. A contender who is a problem on any floor.
narratives.saxon-panchik: Panchik's game is fast and slick: 95th-percentile gymnastics and 88th sprint, with a 2:01 Fran and a 0:52 400m near the top of the field. The longer grind is where he gives a little, Long Engine at 78th, and a 535 lb deadlift near the bottom of reporters marks heavy as the relative soft spot. The model has him 10th, but on a skill-and-speed floor he beats that seed fast.
narratives.colin-bosshard: Bosshard reads as an engine with a thin top end: Long Engine at 68th and a 1st in Open 26.2 to anchor it, but phosphagen down at 27 and Heavy at 28th say the explosive, loaded end is where he leaks. One Games trip, 17th. The model has him 11th among the contenders. His weekend depends on the floor staying long and unloaded rather than fast and heavy.
narratives.tudor-magda: Magda brings real horsepower: a best-in-field 605 lb deadlift, a 385 lb clean and jerk second in the field, and a 1017 double-under count nobody touches. The cost is the tank, Bodyweight at 15th and Long Engine at 25th, so a long aerobic grind is where the field reels him in. Two Games trips, best of 10th. His path up is short, heavy and explosive, not long and gymnastic.
narratives.austin-hatfield: Hatfield is a strength athlete with a real motor: Heavy at 88th and Sprint at 83rd, a best-in-field 1:50 Fran, a 535 lb squat second in the field, and an 83 phosphagen read. The long aerobic grind is the relative soft spot, Long Engine at 60th, so a marathon-style piece is where he gives ground. Two Games trips, best of 5th. Heavy and explosive is where he scores.
narratives.chris-ibarra: Ibarra is steady to a fault: an 83 consistency, the highest kind of mid-pack reliability, with Long Engine at 65th and Metabolic at 63rd his best lanes. The barbell is the relative gap, Heavy at 45th and a thin phosphagen of 34, so a heavy or explosive day is where he slides. Two Games trips, best of 13th. A contender who climbs by out-lasting the volatile athletes around him, not by winning events.
narratives.ricky-garard: Garard is a heavyweight engine: Heavy at 95th and Bodyweight at 88th, with a best-in-field Filthy 50 and a sub-90-second 30 muscle-up time nobody matches. The barbell technique is the relative soft spot, a 205 kg squat near the bottom of reporters, with Balance and Coordination his softest skills. Runner-up at the 2025 Games and a 2022 podium, he is a genuine title threat when the work is long and brutal.
narratives.william-leahy-iv: Leahy is a strength athlete fighting his own engine: a healthy 57 phosphagen and a 43rd-percentile long engine are his best, but a metabolic floor at 15th and a sprint read at 18th drag the profile to a 42 capacity. One Games trip, 26th. The model has him 17th among the contenders. His weekend lives or dies on whether the tests stay short and heavy instead of long and gassy.
narratives.enrico-zenoni: Zenoni is a gymnastics-leaning mid-pack read, 50th on the apparatus and steady at 76 consistency, but the barbell is a genuine drag: a 205 kg squat and a 230 kg deadlift both near the bottom of reporters. Two Games trips, best of 22nd. He needs the tests skill-heavy and the loads light, because a heavy or short-sprint day is where the field leaves him.
narratives.moritz-fiebig: Fiebig is a strength-leaning veteran whose competition output has not matched the barbell: a 260 kg deadlift third in the field and a 220 kg squat are real, yet Weightlifting and Bodyweight both land in the teens on the floor. Four Games trips, best of 19th. The model has him 19th. He needs the tests to reward the lifts directly rather than bury them in skill and volume.
narratives.victor-hoffer: Hoffer's case lives on the longer grind: a 38th-percentile long engine and a 3rd in QF Test 4, with Endurance and Accuracy his best skills. The exposed end is bodyweight, dead last in his own profile at the 5th percentile, and sprint at 10th, so anything fast or skill-light off the floor sinks him. One Games trip, 38th. Give him a long barbell piece and the engine can quietly beat the 20th seed.
narratives.aniol-ekai: Ekai is power over patience: Heavy at 75th and Sprint at 68th, with a 172 kg clean and jerk third in the field. The engine is the clear cost, Long Engine at 33rd and a 19:10 5k near the bottom of reporters, so a long aerobic piece is where he drops out. A high 85.6 consistency and one Games trip at 18th. His path is short, heavy and fast.
narratives.nate-ackermann: Ackermann is a rookie with a loud top end: Heavy and Sprint both at the 100th percentile, the explosive, loaded, short work where he beats the whole field. The hole is the apparatus and the bodyweight grind, the latter at 38th, so a high-skill or high-volume bodyweight test is where he falls out. No Games tape, so the model rides a wide band at #22. Heavy and fast he is dangerous; long and skillful he is exposed.
narratives.nika-maisuradze: A confirmed qualifier with no Games tape, and the bodyweight number is loud: 93rd percentile, with a 9th in Open 26.1 and a 6th in 26.3 backing the gymnastics. The holes are stacked on one side, Sprint and Heavy both at 23rd, so a fast clock or a climbing barbell sinks him. The model lands him 23rd on a low-confidence band. Speed and strength are where the field eats him.
narratives.ben-fowler: Fowler is the flat-line rookie: nothing on the card is a weapon, nothing a hole, with the modal domains and all three energy systems clustered in the low 60s. The model reads that as a 24th seed with a low-confidence band, because flat-and-fine without a separator rarely climbs at the Games. No tape to lean on. He needs one test to fall his way and a clean, mistake-free weekend.
narratives.quinn-robinson: Robinson is a barbell rookie, and the numbers back it: a 500 lb squat fourth in the field, a best-in-field front squat, and Heavy at the 90th percentile. The catch is everything unloaded, Long Engine at 57th and a bench that lands last of reporters telling you the engine has not caught the strength yet. No Games tape. The model has him 25th. He needs a heavy, short weekend to make noise.
narratives.roman-khrennikov: Khrennikov is as complete as anyone in the field: 100th-percentile metabolic, 98th weightlifting and gymnastics, and a 95th bodyweight read, with a 2:00 Fran and a 260 kg deadlift to match. The only soft edges are technical skill, Accuracy and Coordination, and they are minor. A runner-up in 2022 and a 2023 podium, the model's 26th seed reflects a thinner 2026 Open, not the athlete. A contender who can win any event.
narratives.tom-kingdon: Kingdon is an odd, lopsided rookie: a best-in-field overhead squat and strong Olympic lifts, plus a 260 kg deadlift, yet a back squat near the bottom of reporters. Metabolic at 65th is his best domain. The Olympic lifts are a genuine weapon; the grind and the squat strength are the questions. No Games tape, model at 27th. He needs barbell-technical tests, not long ones.
narratives.alex-kotoulas: Kotoulas is a rookie with an endurance lean, Gymnastics and Long Engine his best in the high 40s, but the whole profile sits below the field and a 190 kg squat lands near the bottom of reporters. The model has him 28th on a low-confidence band. There is no obvious weapon here, so his weekend is about clean execution and hoping the tests reward patience over power.
narratives.sven-geens: Geens is a rookie with one lane and two big holes: Bodyweight at 80th is genuinely good, but Sprint and Heavy both near the floor say anything fast or loaded ends his event early. The energy systems all read around 50, a grinder without a gear change. No Games tape, model at 29th. He needs long, moderate, bodyweight-flavored tests, and even then the ceiling is modest.
narratives.bayley-martin: Martin is a speed athlete: Sprint at 60th with Speed and Agility leading the skill read, but the engine is the clear hole, Long Engine at 20th with Endurance and Stamina his softest skills. Two Games trips, best of 12th. The model has him 30th. He scores on short, athletic, fast tests and gives ground the moment the work turns long.
narratives.fabian-hermans: Hermans is a technician without a tank: Balance and Coordination lead the skill read, but Bodyweight sits dead last in the field and every energy system reads in the mid-40s, for a 46 capacity and a 31st seed. A high 88 consistency just means he is reliably back. The control is real, the horsepower is not. He needs a low-volume, skill-precise test to show anything.
narratives.calum-clements: Clements is fast and light: Sprint at 50th and Heavy at 53rd his best, with Agility and Speed topping the skill read, but Long Engine dead at 10th is the hole the Games will find. Two Games trips, best of 16th. The model has him 32nd. Short and explosive is where he registers; a long aerobic grind is where he disappears.
narratives.bjarni-leifs: Thin file, monster squat. No Games tape and a low-confidence #33, but the barbell is loud: a 240 kg back squat third in the field, best on the 3RM and 5RM. The strength has not turned into competition output, though. Metabolic sits at 18th and a 145 kg clean and jerk lands near the bottom of reporters. High ceiling on a strength day, real questions once the work runs long.
narratives.thomas-stroier: Rookie with one trick and a lot of exposure. The bodyweight number is genuinely elite at 98th, with a 3rd in Open 26.1, but everything else is bare: Sprint and Heavy both at the floor and the energy systems in the high 30s, for a 40 capacity and a 34th seed. Give him a pure bodyweight test and he is live. Anything fast or loaded and the field runs away.
narratives.ty-jenkins: Jenkins is a young, light mover: Bodyweight at 40th and Sprint at 38th his best, with Speed and Agility leading the skill read, but Long Engine and Weightlifting both at the 8th percentile, and squat and clean numbers last among reporters. One Games trip, 15th. The model has him 35th. The athleticism is there; the strength and the engine have a lot of room.
narratives.joel-molinia: Molinia is a one-note rookie: Bodyweight at 65th is the lone bright spot, but Sprint and Heavy near the floor and all three energy systems in the low 30s leave him at a 36 capacity and a 36th seed. A high 84 consistency just means he is steadily back of the pack. No Games tape. He needs a bodyweight-only test to register.
narratives.kalyan-souza: Souza is a light, steady grinder: Metabolic and Bodyweight his best in the mid-30s, but the barbell is a genuine hole, Weightlifting at 13th with squat and clean numbers last among reporters. Three Games trips, best of 14th, so the experience is real even if the numbers are modest. The model has him 37th. He needs bodyweight-and-engine tests, not loaded ones.
narratives.henrik-haapalainen: Haapalainen is fast and experienced: Sprint at 57th with Speed and Agility leading, and a 170 kg clean and jerk in the upper half of reporters, but the engine is the cost, Long Engine at 18th with Endurance his softest skill. Four Games trips, best of 14th. The model has him 38th. Short and sharp is where he scores; a long aerobic floor is where he fades.
narratives.dylan-hamming: Hamming is a rookie with a narrow strength lean: Heavy at 68th and Sprint at 65th his best, Speed and Power his top skills, but the whole engine is gone, Long Engine and Gymnastics both at the 5th percentile and a 20 capacity. No Games tape. The model has him 39th. A single heavy, short test is his only window; anything else and the field is far ahead.
narratives.benjamin-reyes: The model parks Reyes #40 of 41 on low confidence, and the file backs it up: his two best domains, Gymnastics and Long Engine, sit at the 3rd percentile off a deep finish in Open 26.3, and Sprint and Bodyweight bottom out at the floor. All three energy systems land around 10 percent of the field beaten, and a 94 consistency says that is where he reliably lives. No Games tape, so the ceiling is a guess, but the current read is thin.
narratives.luis-cuellar: Cuellar sits last at #41 on a 9 capacity, the thinnest read in the men's field: his best domains, Metabolic and Gymnastics, are at the floor and every energy system is in the single digits. A 95 consistency only confirms the level is steady, not high. No Games tape to lean on. This is a developmental weekend; the gap to the field is large across every domain.
narratives.mirjam-von-rohr: Von Rohr tops the women's model, and the engine is why: a 100th-percentile long engine, a 92 phosphagen read, and energy systems that stay high across the board, so nothing falls out from under her. Her softest rooms, Sprint and Heavy, still sit 72nd to 77th, which means there is no real hole to exploit. One Games trip and a 7th already on the card. The number one seed is built on range.
narratives.lucy-campbell: Campbell owns the apparatus: 100th-percentile gymnastics and a 97th long engine, the profile of an athlete who beats the field when the test goes upside down or long. The barbell is the relative soft spot, Heavy at 54th with a 135 kg squat and a 94 kg clean and jerk near the bottom of reporters, so a heavy day narrows the gap. A 2nd-place Games finish says the ceiling is the podium. Keep it gymnastic and she wins.
narratives.claudia-gluck: Gluck is quick and slick: Sprint at 77th and Gymnastics at 79th, the profile of an athlete who scores on fast, technical work, with a 1st in Open 26.2 to anchor it. The endurance side is the trade, Stamina and Endurance her softest skills and Long Engine fading to 62nd. Two Games trips, best of 12th. A contender on a fast, skill-heavy floor; on a marathon day she slides.
narratives.emma-lawson: The file reads like a metronome: #4 of 40 on an 82 consistency, with a 95th-percentile metabolic engine the separator and energy systems sitting flat and high so nothing drops out. Even her softest domains stay elite, Heavy at 79th and Weightlifting at 90th, with a strong clean and jerk to back it. Three Games trips and a 2nd in 2023. The lone soft number is a deadlift near the bottom of reporters.
narratives.kyra-milligan: Milligan is all barbell: Heavy at 92nd and Weightlifting at 87th, with a 340 lb squat third in the field. The flip side is volatile, a 68 consistency among the lowest up front and a bodyweight read at the 5th percentile, so a high-skill or high-volume gymnastics test can sink an event. One Games trip, 22nd. The model still likes her 5th. Heavy days are where she wins; the swingy floor is the risk.
narratives.aimee-cringle: Cringle is an engine athlete who can move load when she has to: Metabolic at 85th and a best-in-field deadlift, with a 2nd in the 2025 Run/Row/Run to anchor the aerobic read. The relative softness is the technical barbell and the sprint, both around the 50s, still respectable. Two Games trips, best of 8th. On a long, mixed floor she is a podium threat; she just needs the lifting kept simple rather than skillful.
narratives.danielle-brandon: Brandon is fast and explosive: Sprint at 92nd, a 210 lb snatch second in the field, the profile of an athlete who scores on short, athletic, high-skill work. The long grind and the heavy barbell are the softer rooms, both in the low 70s, so a marathon piece is where she gives a little. Seven Games deep with a 4th best. On a fast, gymnastic floor she is a podium threat.
narratives.lucy-mcgonigle: McGonigle is a sprinter-mover: Metabolic at 67th and Sprint at 56th, with Speed and Agility leading the skill read, but the barbell is a clear hole, a back squat and clean and jerk both last among reporters. One Games trip, 11th. The model has her 8th. She scores on fast, light, technical work and gives real ground the moment the load climbs.
narratives.grace-walton: Walton is a balanced engine athlete: Metabolic at 69th and Bodyweight at 62nd, with Stamina and Endurance leading off a 1st in the 2024 Firestorm. Nothing is a glaring hole, with gymnastics and sprint just below the middle, so she is more solid than spiky. Two Games trips, best of 14th. A contender who climbs by stacking steady finishes on the mixed-modal work rather than winning specialist tests.
narratives.carolyne-prevost: Prevost is the field's grizzled grinder, with a benchmark card that travels: a best-in-field CHAD1000x, a 330 lb squat and a 405 lb deadlift both near the top of reporters. On the floor the engine carries her while gymnastics and bodyweight are the softer rooms. A high 80 consistency is the veteran tell. Four Games trips, best of 12th. She climbs by never blowing an event, not by winning one.
narratives.leah-st-ren: Storen is the rookie nobody wants to draw: Heavy and Sprint both at the 100th percentile, a 93 consistency among the highest in the field, and a benchmark card that is absurd, best-in-field bar muscle-ups and 5k. The model still flags low confidence because there is no Games tape, and her softest domains, the long engine and gymnastics, still sit in the 90s. An 11th seed that could be a lot higher.
narratives.lydia-fish: Fish is a young strength athlete with a familiar gap: Heavy at 67th with Strength and Balance leading off a 2nd in the 2025 Climbing Couplet, but a bodyweight read at 31st and a phosphagen of 24 that says the very top-end speed is missing. One Games trip, 13th. The model has her 12th. She wins on loaded, controlled tests and is exposed when the work goes light, fast and high-skill.
narratives.madeline-sturt: Sturt is a deep veteran with a strength lean: a 150 kg squat fourth in the field and a 185 kg deadlift second, with Speed and Agility her top skills. The engine is the soft spot, Long Engine at 26th and Endurance her weakest skill. Six Games trips with a 6th best, so the big-stage nerve is proven. The model has her 13th. Short and loaded is her lane.
narratives.morgane-thyssens: Thyssens is a barbell rookie with elite numbers: best-in-field bench and power clean, with Heavy and Sprint both at 97th and a 93 consistency. The tell is the gymnastics-engine side, a 2:33 Fran near the bottom of reporters, so a high-skill or high-volume bodyweight test is the hole. No Games tape. The model has her 14th. Loaded and short she is a threat; long and gymnastic she is exposed.
narratives.var-thurmann-moe: Thurmann-Moe is a powerful rookie: Bodyweight at 97th and Heavy at 95th, with Speed and Stamina leading the skill read off a strong Quarterfinals. The relative softness is the apparatus and the long grind, both in the 80s, so she is exposed more by high-skill gymnastics than by anything fast or heavy. No Games tape, model at 15th. A real threat if the tests stay explosive.
narratives.elena-carratala: Carratala hides a real tool at #16: a 400m run of 1:00, best in the field, so any short sprint window is live, and Balance and Coordination lead her skill read. The barbell pulls her back, Heavy at 8th and a 160 kg deadlift near the bottom of reporters, and long oxidative work, where she beats just 40 percent of the field, is the ceiling. One Games trip, 38th. Keep it fast and technical.
narratives.rebecca-fuselier: Fuselier is a gymnastics specialist with a thin barbell: a best-in-field 1:59 Fran and 86 pull-ups say the bodyweight engine is genuinely fast, but a 285 lb squat near the bottom of reporters and Heavy at 13th say the loaded work is the hole. One Games trip, 30th. The model has her 17th. Give her a high-skill, high-rep bodyweight test and she is live; a climbing barbell and the field pulls away.
narratives.paige-rodgers: Projected #18, and the gymnastics is what can lift her past it: 69th percentile, third on the 2023 Inverted Medley. A bar-heavy floor exposes her, Heavy at 33rd and Long Engine at 46th her softest domains, with Strength and Endurance the gaps. A 78 consistency steadies the projection, and a 2023 top-10 says the ceiling is real.
narratives.siria-meha: Meha is a strength athlete in a field that punishes one-dimensional profiles: Long Engine and Weightlifting her best, with Strength and Accuracy topping the skill read, but bodyweight and metabolic both near the floor and a 39 capacity. One Games trip, 26th. The model has her 19th. The barbell can win her a single event, but the engine and the gymnastics are where the field opens a gap over three days.
narratives.haley-adams: Adams is a pure engine: Metabolic at 97th and Bodyweight at 87th, the profile of an athlete who beats the field on mixed-modal and gymnastic volume. The barbell is the honest weakness, a squat and clean and jerk both near the bottom of reporters, so a heavy day costs her real points. Six Games deep with a 4th best. The model has her 20th, lower than the engine suggests because the loaded tests bite.
narratives.anikha-greer: Greer is a pure sprinter: an 83 phosphagen read and Sprint at 62nd, with Power and Agility her top skills. The model has her 21st, and her whole weekend hinges on the tests staying short, because anything long is a write-off.
narratives.tayla-howe: Howe is a rookie with a clean two-lane profile: Bodyweight at 95th and Heavy at 85th, with Stamina and Speed leading the skill read. The season says she can climb if the tests reward power and bodyweight strength.
narratives.aline-wirz: Wirz is a powerful rookie: Heavy at 74th and Bodyweight at 67th, with Stamina and Strength topping her skill read. She needs short, loaded tests to climb, because there is no engine or gymnastics edge when the work runs long.
narratives.olivia-kerstetter: Kerstetter is a strength-speed threat: Heavy at 90th and Sprint at 79th, with Strength and Power her top skills and a 210 lb squat snatch near the top of reporters. The model has her 24th, well below where a heavy, fast floor would put her.
narratives.jennifer-muir: Muir is a sprinter with a single big hole: a 79 phosphagen read and Strength and Endurance leading the skill list, but Gymnastics at the floor, the kind of gap the Games will find. narratives.bergros-bjornsdottir: At 19 with no individual Games file, the model can only pin her at #26 on low confidence, but the season tape is sharp where it counts: a 100th-percentile bodyweight engine that put Open 26.1 in 3rd, and enough metabolic gas to take a Quarterfinal test outright. The exposure is the barbell and the short stuff, Sprint and Heavy both at 38th. High floor on grind, real questions when the load climbs.

narratives.gabriela-migala: Migala is a fast, complete veteran: Sprint at 90th and Metabolic at 87th, with a strong barbell card, a 155 kg squat and a 115 kg clean and jerk both near the top of reporters. The relative soft edges are balance and coordination, minor for a profile this broad. Five Games trips with a 2nd in 2024. The model's 33rd seed reflects a quieter 2026 Open, not the athlete; she is a clear top-half talent.
narratives.alex-gazan: Gazan is a strength-speed threat: Heavy at 82nd and Sprint at 72nd, with a 255 lb clean and jerk second in the field and a 400 lb deadlift near the top of reporters. The engine is the trade, Long Engine at 31st and Endurance her softest skill, so a long aerobic grind costs her. A 5th-place Games finish in 2023 says the ceiling is high. The model's 34th seed sits well below a heavy, fast floor.
narratives.olivia-geisthardt: Geisthardt is a one-note rookie: Bodyweight at 92nd is genuinely good, with a 6th in Open 26.1, but metabolic and sprint both near the floor and the energy systems in the 30s, for a 40 capacity and a 35th seed. The single tool is real; the tank and the speed are not there yet. No Games tape. She needs a pure bodyweight test to register, and even then the weekend is steep.
narratives.ellie-turner: Turner is a strength athlete with a clear apparatus gap: Heavy at 51st her best with Strength and Power her top skills, but Gymnastics at 10th the hole, and Balance and Agility her softest skills. Three Games trips, best of 18th, so the experience is real. The model has her 36th. A heavy, simple floor is where she scores; a high-skill gymnastics piece is where she loses ground fast.
narratives.miley-wade: Wade is 18 and the youngest in the field, and the numbers read like a debut: a 37th seed at 39 capacity, with gymnastics and the long engine her best in the low teens and the energy systems in the high 30s. Balance and Coordination lead the skill read, the raw material of a future contender. No Games tape. This is a learning weekend, with the ceiling years away rather than this July.
narratives.elisa-fuliano: Fuliano is a strength athlete in a thin overall profile: a best-in-field back squat and front squat and a strong clean and jerk, but Long Engine and Gymnastics both at the floor and a 32 capacity. Three Games trips, best of 20th, so the stage is familiar. The model has her 38th. The barbell can steal her an event, but the engine and the apparatus are large gaps over three days.
narratives.rachel-noel: Noel sits near the bottom at #39 on a 6 capacity: every domain and energy system is at or near the floor, with Power and Strength her best skills but nothing on the card a weapon. A 96 consistency only confirms the level is steady, not high. No Games tape. This is a developmental weekend; the gap to the field is large across the board.
narratives.hannah-black: Black is the field's most lopsided rookie: a best-in-field clean and jerk and squat snatch say the raw strength is genuinely elite, yet every modal domain and energy system sits at the floor, and a 5k near the bottom of reporters shows no engine. No Games tape. The model has her last at #40. Give her a one-rep-max barbell event and she is dangerous; anything with volume or a clock and the field is long gone.
